name: mhs-building-507
estimated: some heights, with a photograph as a reference: the underside of the street face's finned upper storeys and the foot of the canopy's fascia; and the faces no photograph shows, drawn plainly
refs_note: the folder of refs/ that holds the reference views (views.json, masks/), which refine, compare, metrics, sky_mask and the viewer's ?sv= read: refs/photos (gitignored), whose views tools/photo_camera.py writes. Its one photograph is taken at dusk from across the street east-south-east of the south-east block, square to its street face, about 16 m from it, through a lens of about 98 degrees across whose principal point is off its centre (a shifted lens: its verticals are upright); its camera is fitted to the street face's parapet (2 degrees off the frame's axis) and its north-east corner, and to the fronts of the three glazed steps north of it, whose tops the LiDAR gives, held 1.6 m over the LiDAR's ground (rms 0.59 px)

building.title: M&HS Building (507), University of Auckland
building.note: outline: building 507's outer ring from the main project's campus.json, in the map's frame; it chooses the crop box and the building's own points (frame.near_outline, measure and topview). The site replaces block 507 by its id.

origin.note: the campus origin, as in campus.json; the landmark's local metres = NZTM (EPSG:2193) minus the NZTM of this point, with grid north

door.note: before the entrance under the canopy at the glazed steps' foot, which the photograph shows (the campus map records no lobby or entrance in 507, and the OpenStreetMap snapshot no entrance within 150 m: its entrance is not known from a record): on the pavement 2.25 m out from the canopy's front (u 1.0, w 30.0 in the building's frame; (-1.0, 30.0) in the view frame), where the LiDAR has ground (none under and just before the canopy). The LiDAR's ground within 1 m: 7 returns, p10/p50/p90 68.406/68.504/68.592 m

lidar.licence: Auckland Part 1 LiDAR (2024), OpenTopography NZ24_Auckland, doi:10.5069/G9HH6H8T: sourced from LINZ and licensed by Regional Software Holdings Limited for re-use under CC BY 4.0

aerial.licence: Auckland Central 0.06 m Urban Aerial Photos (2023): sourced from LINZ and licensed by Auckland Council for re-use under CC BY 4.0

frame.method: LiDAR building points (class 6) more than min_above m above the ground and within near_outline m of building.outline
frame.thresholds_note: min_above 10 m over the provisional ground, so that the frame is the building's: the low roofs and the street's things are left out; the centre from its points over 17 m (tower_above), its two blocks' roofs. The walls' axis runs along the street face of the south-east block (bearing 198.3 deg, as 501's and 502's walls run), so z faces east-south-east, toward the street the photograph is taken from; all three lowered by 0.47 m with the ground set at the door (step 7), so that they pick the same points

ground_note: the LiDAR's ground at the door (step 7, 2026-11-09); the provisional ground was 68.03 m, the median LiDAR ground in the first crop box, from which the heights in parts/common.js are measured (its H moves them on to this ground)

light.note: estimated: the photograph is taken at dusk, the street face in shade and lit from inside (its windows and its glazed base bright); the model draws no windows and no light inside. The viewer's sun at 108 deg round (square to the street face) and 30 up and an exposure of 1.15 give the building's luma p50 142 against the photograph's 147 (counted in the model's screen box); with the sun behind the building, as at dusk, it is 58 to 72 at exposures of 1.4 to 1.8
